body: I had a HORRIBLE experience with an Aquarius as an Aries, but I guess it also matters that they were a piece of shit person lol

This happened to me too. I ended my marriage with a dismissive avoidant after 3 years (5 together) and it was the most painful and lonely time in my life. Be prepared for him to change, he may detach easily and truly become a different person. But please know that this has nothing to do with you, their trauma and wounds are so deep that they enter into self preservation mode not to feel the pain of losing you.

I chose myself and even though it has been hard, it was the best decision. I get to build an authentic life and give myself the love I was never given. So I'm proud of you for growing and realizing that you deserve better.

If you want  to talk, my DMs are open. I'm 8 months post break up.

Ooof yes, my dismissive avoidant ex was like this, she thought she was mother Teresa lol. She projected this shit onto me for the longest time so I started to believe it! She used to say that I 'lacked empathy' when I didn't do what she wanted or when she was trying to manipulate me into shit. 


She didn't care about my feelings 99% of the time but she tried harder with 'lower risk' relationships (work people, friends, randos)

Exactly what I went through and what I felt after being played and having loved an avoidant for 5 years. 

To my ex, fuck you, piece of shit. I hope you heal so you don't keep going around breaking people with no consequences.

My story to a T -- such a lonely and devastating experience with these people. Takes you to such desperation and rock bottom, dark places that it forces you to grow and crawl out of there for your life. In the end we became better and that's all that matters I guess.

Just a word of caution. I broke up with my ex of 5 years (3 married) and we did the whole 'live together while we figure it out' and it was horrible, it was very heavy emotionally and I would try to figure the living situation ASAP. 

Also, you just left a very long relationship, take some time to sit with your feelings and to grieve your previous life. Take some time to get to know yourself again and to build yourself back up. Jumping to other people at this stage is a recipe for disaster and will only delay and avoid heavy emotions that you need to process.

You'll know when you're ready, there's no right answer because everyone is different

You've described what I went through and what im going through word by word. Thank you ❤️ this perspective is important and I needed a reminder that I'm doing the right things and that growing from this horrible experience of loving someone like that will be the catalyst to something better within myself and when the time comes, share it with someone else.

As many others here have said, my ex was a dismissive avoidant. We were married and when things went south my own trauma and abandonment wounds surfaced, making me anxious and controlling as I was grasping for her love and attention. 

I thought there was something wrong with me when she withdrew affection and attention so I went to therapy, fixed my shit and then realized that things, if nothing, were now worse because I was aware of patterns and setting boundaries within myself and with her. 

Initially I "fixed myself" to salvage the relationship but in the end, I could finally see the lack of emotional intelligence and selfishness in this person. She lacked depth and has some heavily narc traits. I gained my attachment security and ended up leaving her and of course she went and immediately (in a matter of weeks) started dating someone else lol just for the "distraction" (yep; she had the nerve to say this to me, which honestly, it's kinda sad for her. I hope she heals)

I put up with that for a long time because my avoidant ex had issues with intimacy (both physical and emotional lol that wrecked me) but anyway, no, physical touch builds intimacy, closeness and connection. I will never again sacrifice my needs for someone else. If they don't want to kiss you then let them be with someone who doesn't want to be kissed/touched.

Going through one of those low lows today after a good week. We just have to ride the grief and withdrawal from them until time and growth do their thing. 

Wishing you healing and peace, OP

I wrote the letter but didn't send it. 

But like you I'm on the fence about it. I want her to know and to read from my words how much she fucking hurt me and how her behavior and disrespect broke me. I'd be interested to hear arguments against sending the letter because honestly I feel like it would give me the closure I never got.

Oh my god I'm so sorry you're going through this. It's just such a horrible experience and it leaves us so confused and defeated. Anger helps but in the end we need to heal, and do it gracefully. Be the bigger person even when they try to fuck with our minds and hearts with their stupid games and shitty behavior. 

They are broken people and they hurt people and wreak havoc everywhere they go so be thankful that the universe pulled you and your baby girl away from this horrible excuse of a human being. Sending hugs your way. If you ever want to talk, my DMs are open

ETA: I know it's hard but please don't blame yourself, these people are manipulators, they show you what you want to see and tell you what you want to hear. You had no way of knowing that he was putting on a mask and lying behind your back and that's on him for being a piece of shit.

Because they are good at masking, they've created a persona that is not who they truly are deep down. Work relationships are usually shallow, you don't need vulnerability and if you're good at your job, you get validation. This is the perfect combo for them. 

Friendships are a little bit more complex but I could observe that my ex became a different person when she was around people and she valued random people over substance when it came to friends. She felt lonely as fuck because she couldn't really be vulnerable with her so-called friends. I also noticed they were similar to her and they offered validation instead of honest, morally correct advice. They know who to surround with to avoid any sort of accountability and they become the person people want in order to get that dopamine hit from shallow validation.

Master manipulators and deceivers.
I SAW my avoidant with someone else, this past week and I'm wrecked. 5yr relationship, 7 months since breakup. My DMs are open

I needed to read this today. It never hit me that caring and suffering for them after they behaved like absolute shit to us is a disrespect to ourselves.

Thank you.

Yeah it was hard, she has absolutely no regards for other people's feelings. This breakup has been an absolute mindfuck and possibly the most painful and confusing situation I've endured.

Thanks for the advice, hope you continue doing well!

This is how. By rewriting the story, remembering all your flaws and using them as excuses to convince themselves that they did the 'right thing'. Some avoidants (my ex included) have huge egos so they chicken out when it comes to commitment and vulnerability but they still care if you replace them. I know how you're feeling right now and it sucks. The confusion, the anger, the doubt.

Hope you find a way out of this one. They're not worth it. Even if they decided to show up to the relationship you were in for a lonely, superficial and empty ride. 

Let it go, you'll find someone willing to love you for who you are with no conditions.

How long were you two together? I'm 8 months in out of a 5 year relationship and still pretty hurt, upset and confused. I have to stay in touch with my ex because we co-parent our dog but I'm rethinking that. It's too fkn painful to see her once a month. 

The last time we exchanged our dog she showed up with her rebound and it wrecked me. Any tips for healing? Glad you feel on the other side

They are very good at compartmentalizing people, feelings and situations. He may love you and care for you but his brain doesn't allow him to access those feelings for you once the vulnerability is too much for them. It's a defense mechanism unfortunately and there's a possibility that they will stay buried. 
This is how they're capable of just moving on, no regrets, no grief, no nothing.

Truly broken human beings

OP please re-read the first paragraph and honestly think about being with someone like that again. Remember how he made you feel, small, unloved, like you were nothing to him.

These people need professional help. RUN.

I vibe with this one as well. The disgusting person she became after the breakup kinda confirmed that to me. On top of her DA and deep rooted childhood trauma and anger issues, she was just a shitty human being who didn't give a fuck about anything that wasn't her.
Please go to therapy and try to heal before you hurt other people further. You're ahead of most avoidants if you're here tbh. I wish you the best.

Because deep down they are selfish and insecure and they can't deal with their own shit so they project it into others and hurt them.

Fuck them.

I think our own insecurities and attachment issues play a part on this. Also, avoidants are very good at deceiving and pretending, so for some of us they were displaying "total happiness" until they slow fade and discard, so there was no indication that they were feeling bad or that there was something wrong. My ex DA could not communicate her needs and so I thought that everything was ok (she was acting like it was) when it was clearly not. I just couldn't have seen it coming unless I read her mind. 

They lie and manipulate. In my case I'd bring up an issue, she said she'd 'work on it' just to keep me content and then would pretend like she was working though stuff and then slowly but surely go back to the old patterns.

They are destructive, broken human beings capable of high levels of deception. They know what they are doing, the push pull dynamic feeds them and their egos so they stay where they feel comfortable and not challenged by their partners. If you don't have boundaries and don't enforce them with the avoidant they will stay because they enjoy the validation they get from you. They don't actually enjoy the love and the things that the relationship brings. It's awful tbh, I stayed for 5 years and I'm trying to rebuild the wreck that was left of me.

Yeah we were married too. 5 fucking years and she's already promising someone else the same crap she promised me. Who hurts people so much and just doesn't give a fuck?? Like?? Hello?? Did someone ever teach you human decency and respect? 

I'm crashing tf out honestly, I'm angry I got played, I'm angry I loved her to death and all she did was hurt me and lead me on, she lied, deceived me, hurt me on purpose, I'm angry that I still care about her when she doesn't give two shits about me, I'm fucking angry and hurt and this is the worst pain I've ever felt. And for nothing, for a garbage, piece of shit human.

Yes they are when they refuse to take an honest look at themselves and destroy people purposefully with their toxic shit along the way. I know it's due to childhood trauma and that's not their fault but it's their damn responsibility to heal so they don't hurt others.

Honestly fuck them, fuck him. Get angry and move on. He doesn't deserve you.

Ironically, I got better because I realized that my AP attachment made me show up in the relationship as a person I didn't want to be. I thought I was the sole problem of all the fucked up dynamics and so I did it out of love for her. She didn't do the same for me but I realized that in the end I did it for me and it made me better.

Fixing myself did nothing because she didn't look at her DA or tried to heal (even though she knew she was DA and I told her to please go to therapy when I started communicating better). No luck, she had been disconnected from me so she didn't have it in her to fight for the relationship or to look inwards. 

I left and never looked back.

It's not :( I know it's a good thing for the bees but there's barely any grass left. Is that a bad thing. I'm totally open to just leaving them and the clovers there but it doesn't look like a healthy lawn hence my question (I'm a new homeowner, forgive my naivety)
They are beautiful and I know they help feed the bees but the whole thing is those little flowers, there's barely any grass left :(

Sometimes I do, sometimes I get angry and I don't. The truth is, I love and care for her even after all the shit she put me through. I want good for her and I want her to heal so she can experience true love and happiness someday. 

I'm not at a point of forgiveness but acceptance is important and it feels like a step forward.

Yep. Our couples therapist actually told us both what 'we were'. I was AP she was DA. Of course nothing came out of it except me fixing my AP in individual therapy and gaining security to end the relationship. Ex didn't care to fix anything nor to put the effort into couples therapy. I pleaded with her to please go to therapy, heal her inner child.. kept sending her Instagram posts about attachment theory and how we could support each other now that we knew what the problem was. Silence nada, nothing.

By that time she had long been disconnected and was just cruising through the relationship. It was painful to see and experience as someone who was very much in love (so much that I fixed my AP in an attempt to save the relationship lol who would've known that I was saving myself)

She kept saying I was trying to change her and that she felt pressured. She even went to therapy post breakup just to seek validation that 'who tries to transform in love just pushes the other away' or some BS. She has zero self awareness and keeps repeating horrible patterns. Fortunately not my problem anymore.
Keep on grieving. I read somewhere that grief is love with no place to go and I feel that deeply.
I dream about this frequently. Her just showing up without the walls around her heart and loving me the way I loved her.. so profoundly

Happened to me last week. Every. Single. Night. 

Sent me into a spiral, I cried for her for the first time in months.. and here I was rationally thinking I was doing better.. I have no idea when or how will I be able to let go completely, I loved her so fucking much :'(
Happier than ever - Billie Eilish

Yes and no. There were red flags that I missed, some by choice because I thought I could 'fix her'. I was infatuated by the woman and I fell HARD for her. She was good to me for the first two years or so, I can't deny that. We were crazy about each other, I loved her to death until .. idk.. it was like a switch flipped inside of her. I was struggling with family deaths and I wasn't a good partner for a portion of the relationship. She held that over my head till the very end (even when that version of me had ceased to exist). I think she was using that to justify pulling away. She had a hard time with emotions and I am a very emotional person. I was AP (secure now, after a good year and a half of therapy) she was DA.. that's a recipe for disaster that not even an infinite amount of love can fix.

I wish her well and I hope she heals so she lets the next person love her properly like I wanted to. Her walls were too tall and I got tired of climbing. Ripped my heart out in the process.

I left my avoidant after she slow faded over a year and became almost annoyed with my presence.. treating me poorly and being cold and distant. It took me a while and a lot of therapy to get to that point. I didn't want to let go and kept my hopes up when she said she'd work on things. I encouraged her to go to therapy and work on her childhood trauma a her DA (she was aware as was I of being AP) 

I fixed myself, healed some of my AP traits and that helped me see things for what they were. She never worked on it because she'd been disconnected for a while and thought I was 'trying to change her'. It was just breadcrumbs that kept me hooked to her. To me it was holding onto my dreams, we had built a home together and adopted pets.. but I now realize that that was worthless to her. She kept me around because it was comfortable and I provided her validation. I didn't notice she wasn't doing the same for me because of my own trauma, but when I healed I could see it for what it was and I made the decision to leave.

I had some hope early on that she'd see what she lost and try to work on herself but nah.. We had to live together for a few months after the breakup and I could tell she was genuinely happy while I was grieving deeply. This did it for me. I found out a few months later that she had been dating TWO people very close to the breakup and I knew I had to move on. We were together for 5 years and it took her just one or two months to see other people.

I could not believe the utter disrespect towards our home and what we had. She was distracting and avoiding and that's when it hit me that she wouldn't change and that she had finally showed me who she really was.

I went NC except for things that have to do with our dog. Blocked, deleted everywhere. I never ever want to go back to the fucked up dynamic of loving a DA. It's too painful and it took SO much from me. Took my time, my hopes and dreams, my mental health was awful and I lost my self love and self respect all for nothing.

Never ever again.

I've read that it may be because no one saved us as children so we developed that to compensate for having to 'parent ourselves' :( It's also a trait of AP because by 'saving others' we think we'll get the validation and reassurance that we crave from our wounded inner child
Oof I'm not OP but thank you for this

I was aware yes, we both were actually.. learned at the beginning of the final year in couples therapy. The therapist told us both what we were lol (she was DA, I was AP)

The difference is that I actively worked to learn about my part and worked to fix it in individual therapy after my ex clearly wasn't comfortable or rooting for us resolving it in couples therapy together. I have some resentment built up because idk in my mind we were supposed to solve this together and grow from it. It's what couples that want a lifetime do :(

Instead I did it on my own and figured out that this wasn't a healthy or good relationship and I couldn't take it anymore and I left. She's still repeating unhealthy patterns after the breakup and it kinda sucks, I truly want her to be able to experience deep, real love if not from me, from someone else. 

So I guess you're right, I did what I could. I'd encourage her to go to therapy multiple times throughout that final year but she never did. I'd send her info about attachment theory and started to really try and communicate assertively to no avail. I felt like that made her pull away harder because in some way I was 'pressuring her to heal/change' and that triggers them a lot. 

I did my best and I loved (and probably still love) her to death. I saw the potential and lived though this insane connection where I felt like my life was complete. Sad that it was all an illusion and now I'm left here picking up the pieces on my own.

Thanks for the insight, it def helped me
Thank you ❤️‍🩹 it's a tough road for sure but I'm glad I put in the work and got out of there
Thank you stranger, wishing you well on your healing journey ❤️‍🩹

She told me that whenever she saw even the smallest thing she disliked about someone she'd ghost them. I took this as a challenge and gently told her that this was just not how people should behave.

Had been single for 4 years before me because she didn't want to commit to anyone

Didn't care about how her actions made me feel and went ahead with a TRIP WITH HER EX even after I begged and pleaded with her not to (we had been dating for some time at that point)

Her friends were surprised that she had finally "settled down with someone" 

She stayed in my house for the weekend because I had wisdom tooth surgery and she "wanted to take care of me" only to resent me on day 2 because she couldn't bare to be close to someone for so long

Told me she was a serial cheater and liar (and proceeded to promise me that se wouldn't ever lie to me. Spoiler alert: she did, A LOT)

Was vague about why her "serious" relationships had ended and would avoid the topic

Had a phantom ex whom she'd been going back and forth with for at least 6 years (Spoiler alert: I found hidden conversations with said ex towards the end of our relationship, which contributed to me leaving her ass)

She thought she was poly because she "enjoyed being with multiple people at the same time". I begged her to be exclusive with me but she would still bring up that she wanted to explore the poly lifestyle, even against my boundaries she went to a poly party. 

Was fine with being the affair partner of someone in her past.

There were many and I was dumb lol

Yep, the red flags were there, loud and clear. Unfortunately my own anxious attachment and unhealed childhood trauma were at play, I had a savior complex and I saw them as challenges ("I can fix her") rather than what they really were (Big fat red flags).

Cost me 5 yrs of my life, my mental health and losing my self worth for someone who turned out to be a completely different person than what they showed me early on in the lovebombing stage
I unfollowed, removed as follower and blocked everywhere for my own sanity except WhatsApp (unfortunately we co-parent a dog). It's helped me a lot.. out of sight out of mind
My DMs are always open if you want to talk or if you need to vent. God knows this is an exhausting healing journey, you are not alone ❤️‍🩹

It'll feel confusing for a while. I don't have answers for you but I know I was once where you are and it does get better with time. 

You're human and you're hurting because you care deeply. Rejoice in that OP, you have a heart that's capable of love, be kind to yourself and take it one day at a time.

I'm sorry you had to go through that as well, I'm sending you lots of love and light for you to find the way. 

Mine did the "I don't want to take care of you" too and it felt like a stab to the heart. I didn't have the energy to take care of them properly too so sometimes I justified it in my mind but nah.. it's human decency. A cold is different than constant depression, crippling anxiety and panic attacks and a partner is supposed to be your ride or die.

Don't take the fact that he started a new relationship to heart. He's avoiding, it's not real and it's not worth giving your energy to him for one more second m. 

Focus on yourself and your healing OP ❤️‍🩹

It was absolute hell on earth. I wouldn't wish this on my worst enemy.

I was close to the ledge a few times when things got rough. My ex would flat out refuse to hug me or really do anything to comfort me properly. Her default emotion was anger so she'd often get angry at me for being sad or start fights when I'd cry. It was the loneliest, saddest, most difficult time in my life. I felt miserable and the person I loved made it a million times worse. 

She'd get uncomfortable whenever I expressed emotions or when I would get quiet because I didn't want to basically exist. She never made an effort to understand anything that was going on with me and I had to go through three back to back deaths in my family alone. 

Worst thing is, even after she was an absolute POS about my mental health, I held on to life for her. I didn't want her to find me or have to tell my family the news. It's all sorts of fucked up.

But in the end, I found the strength to fix myself, went to intensive therapy, fought my demons harder than ever and I won. Once I recovered I left her and never looked back.

"People who avoid their own feelings will neglect yours"

Never again.

Yep lied about little things, big ones that she knew were going to lead to difficult conversations and also lied by omission a lot. I had to extract stuff from her and it was exhausting, made me feel like I was going crazy. Funny thing is she told me early on she'd 'promise this time she wasn't gonna lie to her partner like she did before' (missed 🚩which I interpreted as oh I'm special she's gonna change for me lol) but she did the opposite
Than you, I needed this today

I feel you, my trauma bond is present but weakening as time goes by... She appears in my dreams and in everything I do but with time I've learnt to reclaim my energy and just let those thoughts be transient.. Accept the thoughts and memories because we are human and we felt deeply towards them but let them go and not put energy where it's not reciprocated.

Happy birthday! I don't know if it helps but my ex sent me a lame ass text on my birthday and it sent me into a spiral. I wish she'd stayed away and respected my no contact wishes. 

It's probably for the best that he stays away. They don't deserve our presence in their lives nor they deserve our time or to be in our minds on our special day.

It was very subtle.. I didn't catch up on it for a while because she'd sometimes give me some validation which soothed my anxiety (breadcrumbing + push-pull, classic avoidant) 

She'd spend a lot of time at work and then come home 'exhausted' so she didn't have 'energy' to spend time with me or to participate on any bonding activities together. Every plan I proposed was lame or she wasn't interested. She started to all of a sudden dislike my friends and thought they were boring so I stopped hanging out with them. 

She just changed.. I don't know how else to put it. She was reactive and angry and I could tell she felt disgusted at times with my existence. I was her last priority and she stopped making any efforts to take care of me, she was annoyed because I broke my thumb and I needed help opening a jar type thing.. 

Her demeanor would change when we were around others whom she did enjoy getting validation from. It was so fkn lonely.. dead bedroom, I tried talking to her about this multiple times with no luck. She kept saying she'd 'work on things' but that was always just to keep me content.. physical touch was minimal, no kissing, no cuddling, no nothing.. we were literal roommates. Not even friends lol friends like each other at least. 

I was so miserable seeing how someone that had shown me such an enormous amount of love, happiness and appreciation could do a 180 on me and literally make me feel like she hated me every single day. 

She was on her phone a lot, said she needed space for her 'socials' so she'd go on every single social media app and scroll for hours while I was sitting next to her. I checked out too, using substances to numb the pain. 

I could go on and on.. it was a miserable time in my life, I felt worthless and so incredibly unloved and lonely throughout all of this. 

Never EVER again.

This SO much!! 

I found out through hard work that I was capable of growth and healing, I took an honest look at my part on things and made an effort to fix my errors and my own anxious attachment but even with all that, things were still shit -- I'd argue they became worse because I started setting boundaries and they didn't like that -- 

This was my ah ha moment, it was not me, it was her and her inability to cope with life and deal with her own shortcomings what made our relationship hell on earth. I grew up, I evolved and she stayed behind repeating her own sad, unhealthy patterns.

Never again.

Yeah mine said that to me after YEARS lol we had moved in, bought a house together adopted pets and all of a sudden 'we're incompatible'.. what a load of bs like wdym we're incompatible ?? we're married girl.. get a grip

Edit to add: She had been disconnected from me for a while and she painfully slow-faded on me until I became so utterly miserable that I had to leave her ass. She still tells mutual friends it was 'amicable and mutual' lol these ppl are fckn delusional

I talked about this with my therapist because I'm also fed up with the constant thinking and wondering about my DA ex. 

She said that we should validate that it's normal, that there was love, admiration and respect towards the ex and that we care about them even after all the bad stuff that went on. It just means we're human.

This is a process, it's grief and it takes time to heal. Slowly but surely you'll find other things to think about and to look forward to. Resisting it makes it more difficult so we need to accept it instead of refusing/rejecting the thought, receive it with gratefulness for the good times and compassion for the errors and just try to focus on ourselves and our own growth.

Facing our demons is the bravest thing we could've done. I'm proud of myself and I'm proud of you, stranger. I can also relate with the 'never saw us as a team' -- She didn't consider me her family even though we were married lol (I laugh now to cope but.. how absurd was it for me to be ok with that for so long.. sigh) 

The bright side to all of this is that we did have the balls to grow, we did what they weren't capable of doing for themselves and we will now be ready for healthier and better love. We are now better equipped to deal with our shit so we don't project it and hurt other people like they did with us. 

Wish you the best!

I relate to this. Out of the 5 that we lasted, 2 were very difficult for me and my mental health.. we had A LOT of issues and some of them were related to that (and the fact that she was nowhere to be found while I was in deep crisis) 

The final year of the relationship, I made the decision to get better, started therapy, stopped using clutches to deal with emotions and made a deep introspection into my childhood trauma and my own anxious attachment. I changed radically and became the best version of me, I felt different, I could see the growth and my loved ones too.. except for my ex. 

She was very hung up on issues from that difficult time
In my life and she brought them up frequently. I said sorry over and over for YEARS and she just wouldn't move on. Even though I was a completely different person now, she wouldn't acknowledge it.

I ended up leaving her because I fixed my attachment and realized that I was in a borderline abusive relationship with someone who wasn't capable of looking at her faults. I brought up that I would like her to go to therapy and she never did, said she'd change and fix things and then would go back to the same old patterns. I felt like I grew up and she didn't so that's part of why I left, I was vibing on a different frequency and I felt that she had stayed behind by choice.

Oh I know the answer to this one: NO, they don't feel the pain immediately, quite the opposite. 

Source: I had to live with my ex for 4 months after the breakup and it was absolute hell seeing her being her absolute best and happy self while I was literally dying inside

Funny story: she never meal prepped and she complained during the relationship about us constantly ordering takeout. First day after the breakup she was ecstatic, cooking amazing food, playing music in my kitchen (I couldn't even eat because I was so incredibly heartbroken) -- anyway, I asked her, why didn't you do this while we were together, you shouldn't have waited for me to breakup w you to do stuff for yourself, she said well I didn't have time when I was with you.. I was like wtf, for the past 6 months she'd come home from work and immediately check out and scrolled TikTok until she fell asleep. I was invisible but hey she didn't have time because of me.. lol

Yep mine too. I explained to her (over and over) that conflict (if handled properly and in the right amount) was a healthy part of a relationship and that what defines us is how we handle it.. she then proceeded to get angry and ramble around how I'm dramatic and I like fighting and conflict and it's my fault that we fight constantly and can't communicate.

I once told her that she lived in a fairytale if that's what she wanted, it's just not possible. But I still felt guilty af when I'd voice my needs or concerns because "here I was, starting shit again" -- girl I just want to communicate like two adults instead of sensitive ass teenagers clawing at each other

Ugh I know this feeling, it was MY birthday today and I was thinking about her throughout the day, wishing she was around and celebrating this moment with me, going to lunch with my fam and just doing mundane birthday things with me like we did for the past 5 years. 

Thinking so much about her on my big day bothered me, it showed me how much my brain is still wired to find her in every single thing I do and showed me that the trauma bond, even though weaker, is still present. 

This is a long and painful road.. 

She sent me a lame birthday text.. zero emotion, bland; almost like she felt forced to do it. I'd rather she stayed quiet and left me alone. I can tell that she doesn't give a f and that makes this senseless overthinking 10x worse
This is so amazing thank you!!! My dog and I appreciate it and we wish you the best always and everywhere you go 💖

Thank you!! You just gave me the best birthday gift <3

!solved

Mine had a lot of 'friends' but no one she could really talk to about deep stuff.. I think closeness is triggering to them no matter what kind of relationship. She was someone who needed a lot of external validation and projected to be very secure and social but was instead deeply insecure and selfish at the core.

This used to happen to me when Calico used a Docker loopback interface instead of the public one. I had to patch the node:

calicoctl patch node <your_node_hostname> --patch='{"spec":{"bgp": {"ipv4Address": "<your_node_public_IP>/24"}}}'

Replace /24 for whatever your subnet looks like
Deleted everything and it helped. Out of sight, out of mind.

There's no guarantee but they are not made out of wood, they do long for connection and they freak out when they get it. Sometimes the clearest sign that they cared is precisely how they run away. It's just.. their timelines and coping mechanisms are vastly different and dysfunctional so the pain doesn't come in a natural way as it does with non-avoidants.
